blocks.md: This lesson covers the book's section on **The Multi-Rate Bridge**. Read the excerpt, then test yourself below.

blocks.source: Vol IV, The Nervous System, § The Multi-Rate Bridge
blocks.md: The running machine joins two computational regimes that run on clocks roughly three orders of magnitude apart. A deep neural network processes camera frames into action proposals over tens to hundreds of milliseconds, with latency that fluctuates from frame to frame. An electric motor drive, by contrast, regulates winding current every few tens of microseconds, in a loop that can never pause because the mass it moves keeps its momentum whether or not a new command arrives.

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Rate tiers from time constants matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: Each tier takes its rate from a different physical constant (winding L/R and the PWM carrier for the current loop, base travel per tick for the permission tick, weight-sweep cost for the chunk policy, prefill cost for the intent model), not from convenience.

questions.q: The section **The Multi-Rate Bridge** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Each tier takes its rate from a different physical constant (winding L/R and the PWM carrier for the current loop, base travel per tick for the permission tick, weight-sweep cost for the chunk policy, prefill cost for the intent model), not from convenience.

The permission path must be the sole writer of every electrical path that can energize a winding, because one unmediated write puts proposer and drives in one failure domain, and the stop itself must be specified in hardware.
A declared WCET is an analytical upper bound on a task's run time on a given processor, distinct from the unknown true worst case and from any measured maximum.

Every interface limit is located at one of five handoffs and one of five limits (latency, bandwidth, heat, determinism, fault isolation) and recorded as a handoff record against the capture-to-brake event timing.
